articles.title: Major US banks are locking out AI agents that log in with customer credentials
articles.summary: Customers are letting AI agents use their credentials to access accounts at Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and other major U.S. banks, sometimes without direct instructions. Morgan Stanley has blocked agents, while other banks are restricting access. Most plan to limit agents to read-only access. The article Major US banks are locking out AI agents that log in with customer credentials appeared first on The Decoder.
articles.author: Manuel Uth

articles.title: OpenAI Shifts Value to $1.25 Trillion as Funding Talks Finalize
articles.summary: OpenAI, which is seeking to raise around $30 billion in a fresh funding round, is now targeting a valuation of $1.25 trillion during the final stages of negotiations, according to people familiar with the matter.
articles.author: Shirin Ghaffary and Rebecca Torrence

articles.title: SK Hynix Pulls Solidigm’s $10 Billion IPO on Regulatory Pushback
articles.summary: SK Hynix Inc. scrapped plans for a potential $10 billion US listing of its Solidigm unit after facing strong opposition from regulators and shareholders, becoming the latest firm to pull an IPO while markets gyrate on doubts about the AI boom.
articles.author: Yoolim Lee and Youkyung Lee

articles.title: OpenAI working on new $30B raise at $1.25T valuation ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Should OpenAI command an over $1 trillion valuation with this round, it would break records as the most highly valued private company ever.
articles.author: Julie Bort

articles.title: JPMorgan’s Mulvihill on AI Concentration Concerns
articles.summary: Aaron Mulvihill, Global Alternative Strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management, said public and private markets are connected as investors reassess the financing risks of the AI and data-center buildout. Credit demand and originations have not slowed, he said, but lenders are becoming more selective: AI-related borrowing must offer returns that justify its cost. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Sure, let’s smoosh SpaceX and Tesla together, who cares
articles.summary: Oh sure, SpaceX's credit risk is pretty high because it's about to borrow another $40 billion to spend on Nvidia chips, but who cares about that? SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss a merger! The degree to which you find this merger compelling likely has to do with the degree to which […]
articles.author: Elizabeth Lopatto

articles.title: Anthropic IPO to Drive Blockbuster Gains for Iconiq, Spark, GIC
articles.summary: By the time Iconiq made its first investment in Anthropic PBC in 2025, the artificial intelligence developer was valued at $183 billion — more than almost any other tech startup in the world — and well on its way to becoming an AI juggernaut. Yet even Iconiq’s later stage bet is now set to bring in massive returns as Anthropic nears its Wall Street debut.The investment firm, which has pumped more than $6 billion into Anthropic, owns a stake worth approximately $17 billion based on the AI company
articles.author: Natasha Mascarenhas and Rebecca Torrence

articles.title: Meta Doubles Down on AI Spending, Plans New Class C Shares
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Meta's plans to boost AI spending and release new Class C shares to ensure CEO Mark Zuckerberg stays in California if a wealth tax is passed. Plus, Tesla reported strong profit, but a big cut to its spending plans is raising questions about Elon Musk's AI, robotaxi and robotics goals for the company as it weighs a potential merger with SpaceX. And OpenAI's models helped find a potentially catastrophic software vulnerability. OpenAI President Greg Brockman and Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince explain how AI is enabling both defenders and hackers. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Tesla Shareholders Likely to Demand a Premium: New Street's Harwood
articles.summary: Tesla investors are likely to demand a premium in a possible merger with SpaceX, says Ben Harwood, New Street Research senior analyst for technology and space infrastructure. Harwood discusses the synergies he sees between Tesla and SpaceX and why demand for Tesla's full self-driving shows the company has momentum to keep profits growing. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: The AI Spending Profit Test, Blackstone's Gray sees "Parabolic" Demand
articles.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Meta tops Wall Street targets, but its AI spending surge raises fresh concerns. Tesla pulls back on spending, while Blackstone President Jonathan Gray pushes back on AI bubble fears. Plus, JPMorgan’s Gabriela Santos and Goldman Sachs’ Ben Snider break down whether the AI boom can deliver profits and where investors find the next winners. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 9 Big Tech engineers building the next wave of fintech
articles.summary: Big Tech engineers are turning to fintech in 2026, targeting workflows like investment research, trading, accounts receivable, and financial data. Using CB Insights People data, we profiled 9 technical founders who came from Google, Meta, Microsoft, AWS, TikTok, and IBM … The post 9 Big Tech engineers building the next wave of fintech appeared first on CB Insights Research.

articles.summary: Noetix Robotics has filed confidentially for a Hong Kong initial public offering that could raise several hundred million dollars, according to people familiar with the matter.

articles.summary: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. articles.title: SpaceX has Blowout Quarter as Musk Floats Merger with Tesla
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down SpaceX's blowout quarterly results and Elon Musk's suggestion that the company combine with Tesla. Plus, Netflix looks to find its next big hit as growth at the streaming giant slows, and a report on Anthropic's draft S-1 offers some new insight and confirmation of the AI firm's financials ahead of its IPO. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Blacksmith hits unicorn valuation after Sequoia leads Series C
articles.summary: Blacksmith, a platform that lets companies build and test AI code more effectively, just announced a $66 million Series C round led by Sequoia that values the company at $1 billion.

articles.summary: Artificial intelligence leader OpenAI Group PBC might have plans to go public in the near future, but it isn’t done with private funding rounds. Indeed, it’s currently believed to be negotiating with investors an additional $30 billion investment that would bring its valuation to a staggering $1.25 trillion, which would make it the most valuable […] The post Report: OpenAI closing on $30B ‘bridge’ funding round to tide it over before IPO appeared first on SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Musk Weighs Massive SpaceX Tesla Merger
articles.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Wall Street splits on AI as Ken Griffin warns of a bubble and Larry Fink says keep building. Musk weighs a $3.5 trillion SpaceX-Tesla tie-up. United warns on rising fuel costs, while Netflix growth slows. Plus, Per Franzen on AI overinvestment, Matthew Condon on Netflix’s next act, and Sagar Gupta joins us on activist opportunities in tech and media. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: SpaceX, Tesla Boards Study Possible $3.5 Trillion Merger
articles.summary: Elon Musk openly endorsed the prospect of combining SpaceX with Tesla Inc. in what would be the biggest-ever corporate merger, uniting assets from electric cars to AI data centers to rocket and satellite capabilities. Bloomberg's Sana Pashankar joined Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss this as well as SpaceX's recent earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Blackstone Nears Deal to Lease London Office to Fast-Growing Fintech Stripe
articles.summary: Stripe LLC is close to signing a lease to take space at a London office owned by Blackstone Inc, as the company seeks to accommodate its rapid expansion.
articles.author: Natasha Voase

articles.title: Exclusive: Slingshot Raises $27M In Seed Funding To Build An Insurer For Those Small Policies Sold At Checkout
articles.summary: Slingshot Insurance, a Minneapolis-based AI-native embedded insurance startup, is emerging from stealth with $27 million in a seed funding round co-led by Rally Ventures and Skyward Group, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively.
articles.author: Judy Rider

articles.title: The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It.
articles.summary: In this guest article from Airrived co-founder and CEO Anurag Gurtu, he contends that Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth does not justify its proposed $2 trillion IPO valuation, given enormous infrastructure commitments, safety concerns, customer concentration and competition from cheaper open-weight models, saying instead that lasting enterprise AI value will come from proprietary data, reliable deployment and measurable customer outcomes rather than expensive models alone.
articles.author: Guest Author

articles.title: Elice CEO Shrugs Off Choppy IPO, Eyes Revenue Boost
articles.summary: Looking past debut turbulence, Elice Group Chief Executive Officer Jae Won Kim aims to double revenue each year by exporting edge data center hardware and capturing sovereign AI contracts. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Nvidia in Talks to Back Firmus After IPO Flop, Information Says
articles.summary: Nvidia Corp. is in discussions to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in Firmus Grid Ltd. after the Australian AI cloud company abandoned an initial public offering, the Information reported.
articles.author: Nick Turner

articles.title: Sam Altman reportedly pitched three endgames for AI safety, one involving a single firm melting everyone else's GPUs
articles.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman laid out three paths to safe AI in an internal presentation: an international watchdog modeled after the IAEA, a merger of the major labs into one entity, or a single company so powerful it could shut down everyone else's compute. He called the last option "terrible." The article Sam Altman reportedly pitched three endgames for AI safety, one involving a single firm melting everyone else's GPUs appeared first on The Decoder.
articles.author: Manuel Uth

articles.title: Anthropic S1 Shows $80 Billion Loss This Year, WSJ Reports
articles.summary: Anthropic PBC could spend $750 billion on additional computing power in the coming years and it lost $80.7 billion in the first half of this year, according to the Wall Street Journal. The media outlet says it obtained a copy of the company's S1 filing as it prepares to go public. Romaine Bostick and Jess Menton report. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AI Fears Roar Back After Elice IPO Flop
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down why fears about the AI trade are resurfacing after South Korean data center firm Elice plunged 32% in its market debut. Plus, Anthropic is in talks with Nscale for a massive new computing deal that could be worth as much as $45 billion, and Eric Schmidt's early Anthropic bet could pay off big, with a stake worth as much as $20 billion if Anthropic hits a $2 trillion IPO valuation. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: ASI Hits $3 Billion Valuation in $325 Million Round Led by Spark
articles.summary: Startup ASI raised $325 million in new funding from investors, allowing the company to expand an artificial intelligence system that helps the military, airlines and air-traffic controllers manage assets.
articles.author: Ed Ludlow and Rebecca Torrence
